system:
You are the analysis agent of a reporting platform for Australia's threatened species. Conservation practitioners — people in government agencies, NGOs and recovery teams who decide where to survey, what to protect and what to escalate — read what you produce. You have read-only SQL access to the platform's database and produce insights from it, each grounded in queries you ran.

# The data

PostgreSQL 17 with PostGIS 3.5. The corpus is every occurrence record the Atlas of Living Australia (ALA) tags as nationally threatened (EPBC Critically Endangered, Endangered or Vulnerable), observed January 2015 to 2026-09-30, from one bulk download (DOI 10.26197/ala.40eee344-07ce-48d2-9ec2-be39574ff4c7): about 2.1 million records, 1,850 taxa, 300+ contributing datasets. Alongside it are all-taxa effort counts per 0.1° cell per month for the same period.

corpus.analysable_occurrences — VIEW — the records to analyse: occurrences that are valid, dated, and not from telemetry (animal-tracking) datasets. Includes population ('wild' or 'managed' — managed means a fenced haven, reintroduction or other managed population, set from the dataset or from corpus.managed_populations) and dataset_kind (the dataset's own kind). Prefer this over occurrences.
  columns: record_id text, source text, source_record_id text, occurrence_id text, harvest_id text, snapshot_page text, fetched_at timestamp with time zone, data_resource_uid text, license text, taxon_concept_id text, scientific_name text, vernacular_name text, national_status text, event_date timestamp with time zone, first_loaded_at timestamp with time zone, decimal_latitude double precision, decimal_longitude double precision, coordinate_uncertainty_m double precision, state_province text, ibra_region text, locality text, geom USER-DEFINED, basis_of_record text, individual_count integer, recorded_by_pseudonym text, occurrence_remarks text, event_remarks text, source_assertions ARRAY, is_valid boolean, issue_count integer, cell_lat numeric, cell_lon numeric, event_day date, managed_by_rule boolean, dataset_kind text, population text

corpus.datasets — TABLE — contributing datasets; kind is 'wild', 'managed' (fenced havens, reintroductions) or 'telemetry' (excluded from analysable_occurrences).
  columns: data_resource_uid text, name text, kind text, kind_reason text, first_seen_at timestamp with time zone

corpus.effort_cells — TABLE — ALL-taxa record counts (threatened or not, telemetry excluded) per 0.1° cell per month: the denominator for reporting rates. Join on cell_lat/cell_lon and month.
  columns: cell_lat numeric, cell_lon numeric, period_start date, period_end date, records integer, harvest_id text

corpus.harvest_runs — TABLE — provenance of each harvest (the corpus download and the effort counts).
  columns: harvest_id text, harvest_key text, run_id text, source text, description text, query jsonb, started_at timestamp with time zone, finished_at timestamp with time zone, expected_records integer, retrieved_records integer, complete boolean, corpus_hash text, request_count integer, warnings jsonb, analysis jsonb, loaded_at timestamp with time zone

corpus.managed_populations — TABLE — curated rules marking managed populations: a taxon in a state (optionally narrowed to an IBRA region and a dataset), e.g. Bilby in NSW, where it survives only in fenced havens, or Woylie in AWC's Mt Gibson haven. Already applied in analysable_occurrences.population.
  columns: taxon_concept_id text, state_province text, note text, rule_id integer, ibra_region text, data_resource_uid text

corpus.occurrences — TABLE — every canonical occurrence record, telemetry included. event_date is the observation instant (timestamptz); event_day is its Australian Eastern local date. geom is a PostGIS Point (SRID 4326); cell_lat/cell_lon are the 0.1° grid cell (rounded to nearest, as ALA assigns them).
  columns: record_id text, source text, source_record_id text, occurrence_id text, harvest_id text, snapshot_page text, fetched_at timestamp with time zone, data_resource_uid text, license text, taxon_concept_id text, scientific_name text, vernacular_name text, national_status text, event_date timestamp with time zone, first_loaded_at timestamp with time zone, decimal_latitude double precision, decimal_longitude double precision, coordinate_uncertainty_m double precision, state_province text, ibra_region text, locality text, geom USER-DEFINED, basis_of_record text, individual_count integer, recorded_by_pseudonym text, occurrence_remarks text, event_remarks text, source_assertions ARRAY, is_valid boolean, issue_count integer, cell_lat numeric, cell_lon numeric, event_day date, managed_by_rule boolean

corpus.taxa — TABLE — one row per taxon (key taxon_concept_id); national_status is the EPBC status ALA attached.
  columns: taxon_concept_id text, scientific_name text, vernacular_name text, taxon_rank text, kingdom text, phylum text, taxon_class text, taxon_order text, family text, genus text, national_status text, status_seen_at timestamp with time zone

corpus.taxon_tiers — VIEW — per taxon: analysable records since 2015, last_record_day, and statistical_tier (≥100 records since 2015).
  columns: taxon_concept_id text, scientific_name text, vernacular_name text, national_status text, records_since_2015 bigint, last_record_day date, statistical_tier boolean

Useful facts: EPSG:3577 (Australian Albers, equal-area, metres) is available for gridding and areas; ibra_region is the IBRA 7 bioregion (null offshore — IBRA covers land only); coordinate_uncertainty_m is the radius the true position may lie within.

**Dates: use event_day** (the Australian Eastern local date) for every date window, count by period and date you report — not event_date, which is an instant stored in UTC and would put early-morning Australian records on the previous day.

# Known properties of this data — read before interpreting anything

- **Records measure effort as much as animals.** These are mostly opportunistic records. All-taxa recording roughly doubled between 2017–19 and 2022–24 (about 1.9×), so counts and range measures grow with effort. Use corpus.effort_cells as a denominator where it matters.
- **Recent months are incomplete.** Datasets reach ALA months to a year late: January–August 2026 holds about 20% of the records January–August 2024 holds, and eBird (the largest dataset) has not loaded 2026 at all. A recent decline is not evidence of anything until this is accounted for.
- **Sources start and stop.** A compilation that ends in 2020, or a targeted survey wound up inside an ongoing state atlas, looks exactly like range loss. Check which datasets carry a taxon's records in each period before calling a change real.
- **Locations vary in precision.** About half the analysable records are located to within 2 km; about a third state no uncertainty; ALA generalises many sensitive species to roughly 10 km.
- **Managed populations** (population = 'managed': fenced havens, reintroductions) are in the analysable view and are not wild trend.
- **National status** is as ALA attached it. Never infer, change or second-guess a taxon's conservation status.
- Taxonomy can shift: a taxon "disappearing" from a region can be a name re-assignment.

# How to work

- Call run_sql with one SELECT (or WITH … SELECT) per call, no trailing statements. Results are capped at 200 rows and queries time out after 30 s, so aggregate in SQL rather than pulling rows. Each call returns a query_id.
- Record each insight with record_insight as soon as it is established. Every insight cites the query_ids whose results support it, and every number in it must be a value those queries returned or simple arithmetic on them. Do not state figures you did not query.
- taxon_concept_id must be copied exactly from corpus.taxa; when an insight is about several taxa, put the main one there (or null) and list the others in related_taxa; region is an IBRA region name exactly as in ibra_region, or null for a national insight; period_start and period_end are the window the insight describes.
- Say how confident you are and why, in the confidence field: record counts, the datasets involved, effort, precision, and any artefact that could explain the pattern.
- When you have recorded everything worth recording, stop.

tools.name: run_sql
tools.description: Run one read-only SQL query (a single SELECT or WITH … SELECT) against the corpus. Returns a query_id, the columns and up to 200 rows. Cite the query_id in any insight that relies on the result.

sql.description: One SELECT or WITH … SELECT statement.

purpose.description: One line: what this query is for.

tools.name: record_insight
tools.description: Record one insight. Every figure must come from the cited queries.

category.description: A short label of your own for the kind of insight.

taxon_concept_id.description: Exactly as in corpus.taxa, or null for a non-taxon insight.

related_taxa.description: Optional: other taxon_concept_ids this insight is about, exactly as in corpus.taxa.

region.description: IBRA region name exactly as in ibra_region, or null for national.

period_start.description: YYYY-MM-DD — start of the window the insight describes.

figures.description: The numbers behind the insight, as returned by your queries.

confidence.description: Why this should or should not be trusted: records, datasets, effort, precision, possible artefacts.

summary.description: One or two sentences a practitioner can act on.

query_ids.description: The run_sql query_ids whose results support this insight.

It is October 2026. A conservation practitioner responsible for Australia's threatened species asks: from this data, what should I know right now — what has changed, what is concerning, what is new, and where are we blind?

Investigate as you judge best and record each insight worth their attention — aim for the most important 20 to 40. For each, be explicit about confidence and about any data artefact that could explain the pattern.

input.sql: SELECT extract(year from event_day)::int yr, count(*) recs, count(distinct taxon_concept_id) taxa, count(distinct data_resource_uid) ds, sum(case when population='managed' then 1 else 0 end) managed FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
SELECT extract(year from period_start)::int yr, sum(records) recs, count(*) cellmonths FROM corpus.effort_cells GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT o.data_resource_uid, d.name, d.kind, count(*) recs, min(event_day) first_day, max(event_day) last_day, count(distinct taxon_concept_id) taxa,
sum(case when event_day>='2024-01-01' and event_day<'2025-01-01' then 1 else 0 end) r2024,
sum(case when event_day>='2025-01-01' then 1 else 0 end) r2025p
FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences o LEFT JOIN corpus.datasets d USING (data_resource_uid)
GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY recs DESC LIMIT 40

SELECT state_province, count(*) recs, count(distinct taxon_concept_id) taxa, sum(case when event_day>='2022-01-01' and event_day<'2025-01-01' then 1 else 0 end) r2224, sum(case when coordinate_uncertainty_m is null then 1 else 0 end) nounc, sum(case when coordinate_uncertainty_m>=5000 then 1 else 0 end) unc5k FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY recs DESC

WITH e AS (SELECT cell_lat, cell_lon, sum(records) eff FROM corpus.effort_cells WHERE period_start>='2022-01-01' AND period_start<'2025-01-01' GROUP BY 1,2),

input.summary: NT threatened mammals have had no ALA records since 2018–2020 because the Fauna Atlas N.T. feed dried up (4,440 records in 2018, 1 in 2024). Black-footed Tree-rat (2,935 records), Melville tree-rat and Carpentarian Rock-rat cannot be assessed from ALA for 2021 onwards. Get recent data directly from NT government.

Of 285 mainly-WA threatened plants, 211 have fewer than 10 records since 2015, and 78 have none since 2022. Do not use ALA to judge trend or extent for WA, Qld or Tas threatened flora.

confidence.reasoning: Effort was summed over cells that hold any threatened record, assigning each cell to a single state, so it is approximate. WITH o AS (
 SELECT taxon_concept_id, cell_lat, cell_lon, date_trunc('month', event_day)::date mo,
  CASE WHEN event_day>='2017-01-01' AND event_day<'2020-01-01' THEN 1 WHEN event_day>='2022-01-01' AND event_day<'2025-01-01' THEN 2 END p
 FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences
 WHERE population='wild' AND event_day>='2017-01-01' AND event_day<'2025-01-01'
   AND data_resource_uid IN ('dr2009','dr368','dr359','dr1411')
   AND taxon_concept_id IN (SELECT taxon_concept_id FROM corpus.taxon_tiers WHERE statistical_tier)
),
rng AS (SELECT DISTINCT taxon_concept_id, cell_lat, cell_lon FROM o),
det AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, p, count(DISTINCT (cell_lat, cell_lon, mo)) dcm, count(DISTINCT (cell_lat,cell_lon)) cells FROM o WHERE p IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1,2),
ec AS (SELECT cell_lat, cell_lon,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE period_start>='2017-01-01' AND period_start<'2020-01-01' AND records>0) cm1,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE period_start>='2022-01-01' AND period_start<'2025-01-01' AND records>0) cm2
  FROM corpus.effort_cells GROUP BY 1,2),
eff AS (SELECT r.taxon_concept_id, sum(cm1) cm1, sum(cm2) cm2, count(*) ncells FROM rng r JOIN ec USING (cell_lat, cell_lon) GROUP BY 1)
SELECT t.taxon_concept_id, t.scientific_name, t.vernacular_name, t.national_status, e.ncells,
 d1.dcm dcm1, d2.dcm dcm2, d1.cells c1, d2.cells c2, e.cm1, e.cm2,
 round((d2.dcm::numeric/e.cm2)/(d1.dcm::numeric/e.cm1),2) rr_ratio
FROM eff e JOIN corpus.taxa t USING (taxon_concept_id)
JOIN det d1 ON d1.taxon_concept_id=e.taxon_concept_id AND d1.p=1
JOIN det d2 ON d2.taxon_concept_id=e.taxon_concept_id AND d2.p=2
WHERE d1.dcm>=40
ORDER BY rr_ratio DESC LIMIT 25

input.purpose: Shorebird flock size per record, eBird+Birdata, two periods

input.category: concerning — migratory shorebirds not keeping pace with effort

confidence.reasoning: Occupied cells and reporting rates come from continuous sources (eBird, BioNet, Birdata, iNaturalist, SA Fauna). With all-taxa effort roughly doubling, a stable species should show more occupied cells, yet several shorebirds held flat or fell. Mean flock sizes per eBird and Birdata record fell for Sharp-tailed Sandpiper, Curlew Sandpiper and Red Knot, but medians barely moved. Mean flock size is sensitive to how observers count and to how many casual checklists are submitted. Structured shorebird counts (Shorebirds 2020 and Birdata) are the proper test.

input.summary: Several threatened migratory shorebirds are not keeping pace with rising effort. Between 2017–19 and 2022–24, Lesser Sand Plover dropped from 95 to 79 occupied cells (reporting-rate ratio 0.79). Curlew Sandpiper, Common Greenshank and Sharp-tailed Sandpiper held flat in occupied cells while effort roughly doubled (ratios 0.79–0.87), and mean flock sizes fell for three species. This is consistent with continued flyway decline and warrants checking against structured shorebird counts.

WITH o AS (

 FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences

 AND ((event_day>='2017-01-01' AND event_day<'2020-01-01') OR (event_day>='2022-01-01' AND event_day<'2025-01-01'))
),
cr AS (SELECT cell_lat, cell_lon, min(ibra_region) ibra FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE ibra_region IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1,2),
e AS (SELECT cr.ibra, count(*) FILTER (WHERE period_start>='2017-01-01' AND period_start<'2020-01-01' AND records>0) cm1, count(*) FILTER (WHERE period_start>='2022-01-01' AND period_start<'2025-01-01' AND records>0) cm2 FROM corpus.effort_cells ec JOIN cr USING (cell_lat,cell_lon) GROUP BY 1),
d AS (SELECT ibra_region ibra, count(DISTINCT (taxon_concept_id,cell_lat,cell_lon,mo)) FILTER (WHERE p=1) d1, count(DISTINCT (taxon_concept_id,cell_lat,cell_lon,mo)) FILTER (WHERE p=2) d2, count(DISTINCT taxon_concept_id) FILTER (WHERE p=1) t1, count(DISTINCT taxon_concept_id) FILTER (WHERE p=2) t2 FROM o GROUP BY 1)
SELECT d.ibra, d1, d2, cm1, cm2, t1, t2, round((d2::numeric/cm2)/(d1::numeric/cm1),2) ratio FROM d JOIN e USING (ibra) WHERE d1>=300 ORDER BY ratio ASC LIMIT 15

WITH o AS (
 SELECT taxon_concept_id, cell_lat, cell_lon, date_trunc('month', event_day)::date mo,
  CASE WHEN event_day>='2017-01-01' AND event_day<'2020-01-01' THEN 1 WHEN event_day>='2022-01-01' AND event_day<'2025-01-01' THEN 2 END p
 FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences
 WHERE population='wild' AND event_day>='2017-01-01' AND event_day<'2025-01-01'
   AND data_resource_uid IN ('dr2009','dr368','dr359','dr1411')
   AND scientific_name IN ('Lathamus discolor','Numenius (Numenius) madagascariensis','Phascolarctos cinereus','Neophema (Neonanodes) chrysogaster','Calidris (Erolia) ferruginea','Botaurus poiciloptilus','Leipoa ocellata','Polytelis swainsonii','Callocephalon fimbriatum','Calyptorhynchus (Calyptorhynchus) lathami lathami','Petaurus australis australis','Dasyurus maculatus maculatus')
),
rng AS (SELECT DISTINCT taxon_concept_id, cell_lat, cell_lon FROM o),
det AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, p, count(DISTINCT (cell_lat, cell_lon, mo)) dcm, count(DISTINCT (cell_lat,cell_lon)) cells FROM o WHERE p IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1,2),
ec AS (SELECT cell_lat, cell_lon,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE period_start>='2017-01-01' AND period_start<'2020-01-01' AND records>0) cm1,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE period_start>='2022-01-01' AND period_start<'2025-01-01' AND records>0) cm2
  FROM corpus.effort_cells GROUP BY 1,2),
eff AS (SELECT r.taxon_concept_id, sum(cm1) cm1, sum(cm2) cm2, count(*) ncells FROM rng r JOIN ec USING (cell_lat, cell_lon) GROUP BY 1)
SELECT t.taxon_concept_id, t.scientific_name, t.vernacular_name, t.national_status, e.ncells, d1.dcm dcm1, d2.dcm dcm2, d1.cells c1, d2.cells c2, e.cm1, e.cm2,
 round((d2.dcm::numeric/e.cm2)/(d1.dcm::numeric/e.cm1),2) rr_ratio
FROM eff e JOIN corpus.taxa t USING (taxon_concept_id)
JOIN det d1 ON d1.taxon_concept_id=e.taxon_concept_id AND d1.p=1
JOIN det d2 ON d2.taxon_concept_id=e.taxon_concept_id AND d2.p=2 ORDER BY rr_ratio

content.text:
I've recorded 32 insights, each tied to the queries behind it. The headline is that most apparent change in this data comes from shifts in which datasets supply records, not from changes in populations. A small number of signals survive that check.

**What looks most concerning**
- **Northern Quoll (Digul), WA:** in AWC's WA monitoring, records fell from 259–838 a year in 11–14 cells (2016–23) to 17 records in 4 cells in 2024, and 56 in 5 cells in 2025. AWC's other WA survey activity held up (278 survey-days in 2024), so less fieldwork doesn't explain it. This is the most credible real decline in the data; ask AWC for site-level results.
- **Regent Honeyeater:** occupied cells roughly halved (44–67 a year in 2017–19, 23–35 in 2022–24). Effort-adjusted reporting rate on continuously running sources is 0.63 of the earlier level, while records rose as observers converged on fewer known sites.
- **Possible, cause unclear:**
  - Painted Honeyeater: effort-adjusted reporting rate 0.59 of 2017–19.
  - Migratory shorebirds (Lesser Sand Plover, Curlew Sandpiper, Greenshank, Sharp-tailed Sandpiper): occupied cells flat or falling while effort roughly doubled.
  - Canberra Grassland Earless Dragon and Konoom (Smoky Mouse): steep drops in occupied cells, but both rely on single monitoring programs. Check with the survey teams before escalating.

**What's new**
- **Elusive Bush-pea:** first records since 2015, from October 2024, at one or two sites in the Sydney Basin. It needs site protection.
- **Plains-wanderer:** recorded in the Mitchell Grass Downs (western Qld) since August 2024, by 3 observers on 11 days.
- **Needs expert checking:** 47 Lax Leek-orchid records from one observer over two days in September 2026, and Eltham Copper Butterfly in a new region, reported by only two observers.
- **New managed populations:** Woylie and Numbat on the Eyre/Yorke Peninsula; Shark Bay Burrowing Bettong and Chuditch in the Simpson–Strzelecki Dunefields.

**What's misleading**
- **Datasets that stopped:** the steepest declines nationally (sawfish, snubfin dolphin, Pacific Ridley, Spotted Handfish, NT mammals) all trace to datasets that ended, including the NT Fauna Atlas, which fell from 4,440 records in 2018 to 1 in 2024. Their status since about 2019 is unknown from this data.
- **Victoria:** the state atlas cut its threatened-bird records about tenfold after 2019, which creates false declines for Victorian birds and invertebrates.
- **Grey-headed Flying-fox:** summed counts fell about 100-fold in 2023 while record numbers held, which points to a lost count stream, not lost animals.
- **Survey timing:** Needle Wattle looked collapsed in 2022–24, then 2025 surveys logged more records than any earlier year.
- **Biggest "increases":** these follow survey attention, not recovery (Scrub Turpentine, Native Guava, Greater Glider, Tasmanian Devil).
- **Duplicates:** about 47% of records repeat the same taxon, day and site, so count distinct sites or months, not records.
- **Stable:** Swift Parrot, Eastern Curlew, Australasian Bittern and Superb Parrot keep pace with rising effort.

**Where you're blind**
- **2025–26:** trends should stop at 2024. eBird ends in August 2025, and only 31 datasets have contributed anything for 2026.
- **WA locations:** 99% of WA records are located only to about 10 km.
- **Threatened plants outside NSW:** 954 WA plant records in 2022–24 against 83,235 in NSW. Of 285 mainly-WA threatened plants, 211 have fewer than 10 records since 2015.
- **Queensland and Tasmania:** non-bird records are thin in both states; 75% of Queensland's threatened records are eBird birds.
- **Arid and northern regions:** for example, 6 records from the Tanami and 11 from Central Arnhem in 2022–24.
- **Wild populations of havened mammals:** Bilby has 123,933 managed records against 352 wild.
- **Sensitive species:** Southern Corroboree Frog has 1 record, and it is misplaced; Gilbert's Potoroo has 3 and Night Parrot 12.
- **Subspecies listings:** NSW BioNet contributes no records for Spotted-tailed Quoll or Yellow-bellied Glider under their listed subspecies.
- **Critically endangered taxa overall:** 178 of 392 have fewer than 10 records since 2015.
- **Recent picture:** for the last 13 months, 79% of records come from iNaturalist and NSW BioNet, and iNaturalist is the only source for 628 of the 1,159 taxa recorded.

Two slips in the recorded insights: the sensitive-species insight wrongly lists Lyon's Soil-crevice Skink as a related taxon, and a few of them leave the region field blank instead of naming an IBRA region.
